title: Number of Insurance Claim Repairs Repair Orders a Customer May Hold
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold any number of Insurance Claim Repairs repair orders, across vehicles and claims; there is no customer-level cap. The limit that does exist is set per insurer claim number and vehicle, by the rule that allows one open repair order for one claim number on one vehicle.

### Questions answered by the rule

**A customer already has one claim repair order open on a sedan. May a second repair order be opened for the same customer's pickup truck under a different claim?** Yes. The number of repair orders a customer holds is not capped; the vehicles and claims are different.

**A customer has repair orders open under three different claims. Does the count of repair orders the customer holds stop a fourth?** No. There is no customer-level cap; only the per-claim, per-vehicle limit applies.

**Is there any figure for the most repair orders one customer may hold?** No. The rule sets no such figure at the customer level.

| Question about the customer | Limited by this rule? |
|---|---|
| How many repair orders the customer holds in total | No — any number |
| How many vehicles the customer has in repair under claims | No — any number |
| How many open repair orders one claim number has on one vehicle | Not by this rule; the per-claim, per-vehicle limit governs it |
